findings.text: System-wide softlockup touch marks every CPU in the allowed mask with a deferred-report sentinel and notifies the workqueue watchdog for that CPU, permitting callers in interrupt context.

External hrtimer tuning interface records a sample threshold derived by scaling the supplied period upward, ensuring the hrtimer fires at least once inside the real watchdog window and guarding the NMI path against turbo-induced false positives.
Hotplug entry points enable or disable the per-CPU detector when the target CPU belongs to the allowed mask, otherwise leaving state unchanged and reporting success.
Public reconfiguration wrappers apply mask and threshold changes with mutex protection in full builds and without it in minimal builds, while soft poweroff provides an unconditional global disable.

Softlockup limit is twice the base threshold and the sampling period spreads that limit evenly across the configured sample windows, converted to nanoseconds; timestamps are a coarse right-shifted running clock comparable across touch and report fields.

Per-CPU utilization tracking keeps a ring of recent windows for system, softirq, hardirq and idle classes using reduced-precision counters, capping each window at full utilization to hide quantization overshoot and advancing a tail pointer each sample.
Hardirq storm diagnosis maintains a small ordered list of busiest interrupt numbers by insertion with swapping, reporting only valid entries in rank order when a snapshot is active.
Interrupt tally record pairs a signed interrupt identifier where negative means empty with an unsigned count accumulated since snapshot, forming fixed-size sorted arrays for top talkers.
Hardirq storm threshold constant equals 50 [CITED].
Reported top hardirq entries constant equals 5 [CITED].
Upper bound constant for threshold sysctl equals 60 [CITED].

Interrupt counting is armed once per storm by taking a kernel IRQ snapshot guarded by a per-CPU taken flag, stays armed while recent hardirq share exceeds the storm threshold, and disarms when share subsides or the per-CPU service function runs; alternate build variants force counting off with no-op operations.

Detector lifecycle initializes completion state, starts a pinned monotonic hrtimer before enabling hardlockup detection, and reverses order on disable by stopping hardlockup first then cancelling the timer and waiting for completion; global start and stop walk the allowed mask invoking per-CPU transitions, while reconfiguration serializes hardlockup stop, soft stop, threshold commit, period refresh, enablement update, soft start and hardlockup start.

Softlockup evaluation requires global enablement and a nonzero threshold, using three escalating horizons within the limit for storm arming, scheduler ejection signalling, and warning emission with duration measured from last touch.

Periodic hrtimer handler skips when disabled or during panic, kicks hardlockup tracking, refreshes a one-shot per-CPU service request, advances the timer, refreshes utilization, honors a deferred-report sentinel with optional scheduler tick sync, and otherwise emits a single consolidated warning with CPU state, module and trace context plus optional all-CPU backtraces, tainting and possible panic on repeated overruns.

Control interface exposes combined, hard-only, soft-only, threshold and mask knobs that validate integer or bitmap input, synchronize reads against live enablement, and trigger reconfiguration only on genuine writes, rejecting hard enablement when unavailable.

Sysctl descriptor table binds user-visible names for watchdog control, thresholds, masks, panic policy and backtrace options to backing variables with access modes and min-max bounds, registered under the kernel namespace at init except in no-op builds.

Global reconfiguration and all sysctl mutations serialize on a dedicated mutex, with inner CPU hotplug read protection during stop-start sequences; threshold commit uses atomic read to avoid mixing old intervals with new limits.

Global touch deliberately avoids the reconfiguration mutex because it may run in interrupt context, accepting races on the allowed mask and timestamps whose worst effect is a delayed check; VM pause and NMI touches can invalidate timestamps and are mitigated by explicit pause clearing and single-copy reads.

Concurrent all-CPU backtrace dumps are suppressed by a test-and-set guard so only one CPU reports at a time, and repeated threshold overruns scale toward configured panic action for soft and hard paths.

Deferred initialization probes hardlockup support in workqueue context, logging distinct messages for unsupported versus failed probes and permanently disabling hard detection on failure, otherwise marking availability and running normal setup once.

Per-CPU service routine refreshes touch time, disarms storm counting, signals completion and succeeds, paired with timer-side rearming that issues a one-CPU synchronous request only when prior completion is observed.
